run.question: In Loki, run the query `{service="checkout"}` against namespace app-282 and tell me how many error-level log lines come back. If the selector returns nothing, find the right one.

report.summary: The literal selector {service="checkout"} matches nothing in Loki; the checkout streams in namespace app-282 carry the label acme_service="checkout" (plus job="checkout-logs", filename="/var/log/checkout.log", level, namespace, pod). Counting over the authorized 24h window (2026-11-20T05:30:57Z to 2026-11-21T05:30:57Z), checkout in app-282 emitted 4 ERROR-level lines out of 16 total lines (10 INFO, 2 WARN), all from pod checkout-698c8f5df-cmddj. The four ERROR messages concern a refused payment token, an inventory-check timeout, an orders-table deadlock and exhausted webhook retries. Aggregating all of namespace app-282 by acme_service and level returned only acme_service=checkout series, so no other service label value shows log lines in that namespace and window.

claims.text: With the corrected label, sum(count_over_time({namespace="app-282",acme_service="checkout"} | json | level="ERROR" [24h])) evaluated to 4 over the window 2026-11-20T05:30:57Z–2026-11-21T05:30:57Z, i.e. exactly 4 error-level log lines were counted.

The same stream total over the window is 16 lines: sum(count_over_time({namespace="app-282",acme_service="checkout"}[24h])) = 16, and the per-level breakdown is acme_service=checkout level=ERROR 4, level=INFO 10, level=WARN 2.

sum by (pod) (count_over_time({namespace="app-282",acme_service="checkout"} | json | level="ERROR" [24h])) returned a single series, pod="checkout-698c8f5df-cmddj", with value 4, so all 4 error-level lines came from that pod.

The returned checkout stream is labelled acme_service=checkout, job=checkout-logs, filename=/var/log/checkout.log, namespace=app-282, pod=checkout-698c8f5df-cmddj, with a level label per line; no label named service appears on any returned stream.

The four ERROR lines returned in the sample are, verbatim in message field: 'Payment processor refused: invalid token (txn 9d1f)', 'Inventory check timed out for SKU-77481', 'Order persistence failed: deadlock on orders table', and 'Webhook delivery exhausted retries for partner ACME', all at 2026-11-21T05:30:21.5214Z–05:30:21.5218Z with level=ERROR.

Aggregating the whole namespace, sum by (acme_service, level) (count_over_time({namespace="app-282"}[24h])) returned only acme_service="checkout" series (ERROR 4, INFO 10, WARN 2); no other acme_service value was returned for namespace app-282 in this window.

The ERROR messages (refused payment token, inventory timeout, orders-table deadlock, webhook retries exhausted) point to failing downstream dependencies of checkout (payment processor, inventory/SKU lookup, orders database, partner webhook endpoint), but no dependency-side telemetry was queried in this Run, so which dependency is at fault is not established here.

gaps: The exact query {service="checkout"} (also tried as {service="checkout",namespace="app-282"}) returned no streams (status no_data) over 2026-11-20T05:30:57Z–2026-11-21T05:30:57Z; this only shows that query matched nothing. The streams actually returned in app-282 use acme_service, not service, as the service label.

The line query {namespace="app-282"} | json | level="ERROR" with limit 500 timed out (TOOL_TIMEOUT) and returned no lines, so individual error lines beyond the 16 newest lines already returned were not enumerated; the 4-error count rests on the count_over_time metric queries, not on the full line list.

Whether the 4 ERROR lines are confined to a single burst or repeat across the window was not resolved: only the whole-window count and the newest sample lines are known, no per-time-bucket breakdown was run.
The dependencies named in the ERROR text (payment processor, inventory service, orders database, partner ACME webhook) were not investigated in this Run, so their health is unknown.
Change history is not an integrated source in this Run, so no change/correlation evidence for these errors exists.
next_steps: Confirm the canonical Loki label for services in this source (acme_service here) before writing dashboards or alerts that use service.

If the error burst timeline matters, run a count_over_time series with a short range (e.g. 5m steps) for {namespace="app-282",acme_service="checkout"} | json | level="ERROR" and compare against an earlier baseline window.
Correlate the payment-refused, inventory-timeout and orders-deadlock errors with the payment, inventory and database telemetry before attributing a cause to any dependency.
